data.name: Atarah
data.gender_notes: Atarah is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word ‘atar’, meaning joy or gladness. In the Bible, Atarah is a feminine form of the name Atar, which is associated with the Ark of the Covenant and the glory of God. The name Atarah carries the meaning “Joy, Gladness” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Atarah usually hope their child will grow to embody joy, gladness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of the joy and gladness found in the presence of God.
data.etymology: Atarah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Joy, Gladness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Atarah total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Atarah, though not explicit in the Christian tradition, can be connected to Old Testament roots, infusing it with a rich historical and cultural meaning. Its association with the Ark of the Covenant, a symbol of divine protection and presence in Jewish and Christian traditions, can impart the sense of being guarded and blessed.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Atarah embodies the idea of divine joy and gladness. It reminds us of the profound, inexhaustible joy found in a relationship with God. Atarah is a name that inspires rejoicing in the Lord, celebrating His love and goodness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Atarah may be interpreted as "Mother of Joy" or "Delight of the Lord," reflecting the Christian belief in the joy and happiness God brings to his children. This name also symbolizes the maternal love and care God provides, nurturing His followers with His grace and presence.

biblical_reference.note: although not directly mentioned, the concept of a crown is biblically significant

historical_references.reference: Atarah was the name of a princess mentioned in the Old Testament book of Jeremiah. She is the daughter of Judea's king, Jehoiakim, and was married to King Zedekiah of Judah. When Jeremiah prophesied the coming Babylonian invasion, Atarah and her brother, Jehoiachin, were taken captive to Babylon in 597 BCE.
historical_references.context: Old Testament, Jerusalem, Judea, Jeremiah, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah, Babylonian invasion

historical_references.reference: In the New Testament, Atarah is mentioned as a descendant of King David in the genealogy of Jesus. Her name appears in the list between the names of Heli and Joseph, the putative father and adoptive father of Jesus, respectively. Atarah's father was named Josiah, and she is believed to have lived during the late 6th or early 5th century BCE.
historical_references.context: New Testament, Jesus, King David, genealogy

modern_usage.modern_context: The Christian name Atarah is seen in various modern contexts, often associated with spirituality, creativity, and the divine feminine. In Neopaganism and Wicca, Atarah is sometimes used as a personal name or honorific title for goddess figures. In contemporary fantasy literature and media, Atarah can be found as a character name or as a title for a goddess or other supernatural entity. In New Age spirituality, Atarah is sometimes used as a name for meditation groups, healing practices, or other spiritual gatherings. The name Atarah holds a deep resonance with those seeking connection to the divine feminine and the creative forces of the universe.

name_in_real_life.story: Mary Atarah from London, United Kingdom embodies the meaning of Atarah - "Joy, Gladness". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
